title: Concurrency-Informed Orchestration for Serverless Functions
problem: Serverless FaaS platforms suffer excessive cold starts because existing container keep-alive policies ignore concurrent invocations: they fail to reason about whether reusing a busy container (delayed warm start) or cold-starting a new container is preferable, and they make imbalanced eviction decisions that prematurely evict soon-to-be-reused containers.
motivation: Concurrent function invocations are pervasive in production FaaS workloads, yet state-of-the-art keep-alive policies treat each invocation independently, causing unnecessary cold starts and latency inflation.
method: CIDRE is a container orchestration algorithm that combines fine-grained container-level state (busy/idle, time-to-free) with coarse-grained concurrency signals to speculatively decide between a delayed warm start and a cold start under concurrent scaling. For eviction, CIDRE uses both container-level recency and concurrency-aware reuse probability to produce balanced eviction decisions that avoid removing containers still likely to be reused. The algorithm is evaluated on two production FaaS workload traces.
key_novelty: CIDRE is the first FaaS keep-alive policy to explicitly model container concurrency state and use it to make speculative warm-vs-cold-start decisions and balanced eviction choices simultaneously.
contributions: Identification of two new concurrency-driven challenges in FaaS keep-alive: delayed warm start tradeoff and imbalanced eviction
CIDRE algorithm combining fine-grained container and coarse-grained concurrency information for orchestration
Up to 75.1% reduction in cold start ratio and 39.3% reduction in average invocation overhead

metrics.speedup: up to 39.3% average invocation overhead reduction
metrics.other: up to 75.1% cold start ratio reduction vs state-of-the-art keep-alive policies

limitations: Evaluated on only two production workload traces; generalization to highly heterogeneous function mixes with extreme concurrency spikes not shown.
